title: nextDraftId and nextPlanningId (milestone/decision ids) allocate from the working tree only, same collision shape QCLI-279 fixed for tasks -- now reproduced live on a decision id
description:
QCLI-279 fixed refs-aware allocation for ONE member of a family of three id allocators in src/cli/main.ts; the other two still allocate from the current working tree's .quest/ contents alone, with the exact same collision shape.

Root cause, unchanged from QCLI-279's own framing: an id allocator's notion of "next" is only as complete as the tree in front of it. .quest/ is committed per-branch like any other tracked directory, so any repo with an in-flight branch (or a detached HEAD behind a moved branch) can mint a duplicate id just by allocating from a different ref. QCLI-279 fixed this for task ids specifically -- nextTaskId (main.ts) now takes the max of the working-tree scan and a new highestSequenceOnOtherRefs helper (GitPort.listRefs, a for-each-ref listing across local heads + remote-tracking refs, not a history walk) that scans .quest/tasks, .quest/completed and .quest/archive/tasks on every other ref. That fix was deliberately scoped to tasks only, on the evidence available at the time -- QCLI-279's own notes explicitly left nextDraftId/nextPlanningId unfixed pending a real reproduction, rather than silently widening the fix without one.

That reproduction now exists. Live, 2026-09-14, during the OPAG-142 0.7.0 campaign: an implementer subagent building QCLI-284 ran `quest decision create` from a branch cut from origin/dev before this session's own `quest decision create` (recording DEC-3) had landed there. Both allocated the id DEC-3 independently -- the coordinating session's DEC-3 landed on dev first (PR #79, commit 9a57c4f); the implementer's own DEC-3 collided the moment its branch fast-forwarded onto the new dev tip. Recovered cleanly (discarded the stale local .quest/planning.json diff, fast-forwarded, re-ran quest decision create, got DEC-4 correctly) -- no data lost, but the collision was real and would not have been caught by a less careful actor.

Two allocators share the unfixed shape, both in src/cli/main.ts:
- nextDraftId (~line 793): scans tasks.listDrafts(true) off the working tree only, mints D-<n+1>.
- nextPlanningId (~line 981): scans planning.listMilestones(true)/listDecisions() off the working tree only, mints M-<n+1> or DEC-<n+1> -- this is the one that just collided.

QCLI-279's highestSequenceOnOtherRefs helper and GitPort.listRefs already exist and are refs-agnostic about what they scan (they take a root and a marker/path set); extending nextDraftId/nextPlanningId to use the same mechanism is very likely a matter of pointing them at the right .quest/ subpaths (drafts' storage location; planning.json's milestone/decision id namespaces) rather than inventing anything new -- confirm this by reading the actual QCLI-279 implementation before assuming it drops in unchanged.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A decision is made and recorded on whether nextDraftId and nextPlanningId get the same refs-aware fix as nextTaskId (QCLI-279), a different fix, or an explicit reason to leave them as-is -- given the live DEC-3 collision reproduction, leaving them unfixed needs a real justification, not silence

If refs-aware allocation is chosen, it is implemented for draft ids and for both milestone and decision ids (nextPlanningId covers both via the same prefix parameter), demonstrated with a reproduction of the collision this task documents (or one deliberately constructed the way QCLI-279's own test suite did) failing pre-fix and passing post-fix

The chosen behavior is documented in the relevant quest instructions guide (task-creation already carries QCLI-279's refs-aware guarantee for tasks; extend or cross-reference it) so an agent creating a draft, milestone, or decision understands what guarantee it does or does not have
bun run check exits 0 with the new/updated tests included

plan: 1. Parameterize highestSequenceOnOtherRefs with the subdirectory set (required, not defaulted) so the scanned family is visible at every call site; add DRAFT_RECORD_SUBDIRECTORIES and thread git+root into nextDraftId

2. Add a separate highestPlanningSequenceOnOtherRefs that reads .quest/planning.json per ref via GitPort.readBlob -- a filename scan cannot work on a single-file store and would return 0, a wrong answer indistinguishable from a right one
3. Filter by prefix family in both, degrade to 0 on any failure, and update both call sites in runQuest
4. Tests modelled on test/qcli279-refs-aware-task-id-allocation.test.ts: sibling-branch and detached-HEAD shapes for drafts, milestones and decisions, plus the non-Git degradation case
5. Mutation-localise the suite: predict which cases each mutant reddens from the test file before running
6. Document the guarantee in quest instructions task-creation, which today promises it for tasks in a way that reads as covering all four id families
7. Record the decision (AC1), add a CHANGELOG entry, bun run check exits 0
implementationNotes:
MECHANISM SURVEY FOR WHOEVER PICKS THIS UP, done 2026-09-16 by a session that did NOT implement it -- read as a starting point, not as a design decision. Everything below was read from the source at dev 87e7bb3; nothing was run.

THE TWO HALVES NEED DIFFERENT MECHANISMS, and that is the thing the task description assumes away when it says extending the existing helper "is very likely a matter of pointing it at the right subdirectories".

1. DRAFTS -- yes, the existing helper very likely does work. highestSequenceOnOtherRefs (src/cli/main.ts:878) already takes a root and a marker, scans one subdirectory set per ref via git.listFiles, and parses the id out of the FILE NAME. Its only coupling to tasks is the module-level constant TASK_RECORD_SUBDIRECTORIES = ["tasks","completed","archive/tasks"] (:856), hardcoded in the body. Drafts are stored one-record-per-file under .quest/drafts and .quest/archive/drafts (src/adapters/workspaces/local-workspaces.ts:166-168 enumerates both), so the same filename scan applies. Lift the subdirectory set to a parameter defaulting to the task set, and pass a draft set.

2. MILESTONES AND DECISIONS -- the helper does NOT work, and would fail silently if pointed at them. Planning records do not live one-per-file: there is a SINGLE .quest/planning.json holding {"milestones":[...],"decisions":[...]} (confirmed against this repository own .quest/). A filename scan over that path finds exactly one file named planning.json, which matches no marker, so highestSequenceOnOtherRefs returns 0 for every ref -- and 0 is indistinguishable from "no other ref carries a higher id". THE HELPER WOULD RETURN A WRONG ANSWER THAT LOOKS LIKE A CORRECT ONE. It needs a content read per ref, not a listing.

The port already has what that needs and NO PORT CHANGE IS REQUIRED: GitPort.readBlob(repositoryPath, revision, path) (src/ports/git.ts:68-74) is a revision-pinned blob read returning null when absent, implemented in local-git.ts. So the planning half is: for each ref from git.listRefs, readBlob(root, ref, ".quest/planning.json"), JSON.parse, scan both arrays ids for the prefix, take the max.

THREE THINGS TO GET RIGHT, all of which the task half already solved and a fresh implementation can get wrong:
- Parse failures must degrade to 0, not throw. The existing helper wraps everything in try/catch returning 0 specifically so a non-Git .quest directory, an absent Git binary, or a ref whose tree lacks the path keeps today local-only behaviour exactly (see its doc comment at :858-877). A malformed planning.json on some unrelated stale branch must not break allocation on this one.
- Only the prefix own family may advance the counter. nextTaskId comments this at :914-916: a foreign-prefixed id must never perturb the sequence. nextPlanningId takes prefix "M" or "DEC" and both live in the SAME file, so the scan has to filter by prefix rather than take the max of everything it finds.
- readBlob is per-ref-per-path, so the planning half is one git invocation per ref where the task half is one per ref per subdirectory. Refs here are for-each-ref tips only, never a history walk, so this stays bounded -- but it is worth confirming against a repo with many remote-tracking refs before calling it free.

CALL SITES TO CHANGE: nextDraftId (main.ts ~:793, currently takes only `tasks`) and nextPlanningId (~:981, currently takes `planning` and `prefix`). Both will need the git port and root threaded in, exactly as nextTaskId already has them (:909-913). Check every caller of both.

ON AC2 REPRODUCTION: QCLI-279 test suite (test/qcli279-refs-aware-task-id-allocation.test.ts) is the model to copy rather than invent -- it constructs the collision deliberately rather than relying on the live DEC-3 incident, which is the right call since the incident is not reproducible on demand.

ON AC3: quest instructions task-creation already carries the refs-aware guarantee for TASK ids. Whatever is decided, that guide is where an agent looks, and it currently promises the guarantee in a way a reader may generalise to drafts and decisions -- so it needs editing even if the answer is "no fix", because today it is silent in a direction that reads as reassuring.

CITATION REFRESH, 2026-09-16, by the session that wrote the survey above and did not implement the task. Two of its four line citations aged out the same day, and the two that held are the load-bearing ones -- so re-measure each clause rather than discounting the whole survey.

The survey was read at dev 87e7bb3. dev is now 89f797a. QCLI-297 (bdf4b61) added 40 lines to src/cli/main.ts, which moved the two CALL SITES the survey tells you to change:

  nextDraftId      survey said ~793   now 949
  nextPlanningId   survey said ~981   now 1139

Still exactly right, verified by grep at 89f797a:

  TASK_RECORD_SUBDIRECTORIES      :856
  highestSequenceOnOtherRefs      :878
  GitPort.readBlob                src/ports/git.ts:70

Nothing in the MECHANISM half changed: drafts are still one-record-per-file, planning records still share a single .quest/planning.json, and the claim that a filename scan over planning.json returns 0 for every ref -- a wrong answer indistinguishable from a correct one -- is untouched by QCLI-297. QCLI-297 changed removal semantics in the fold and in updatedMilestoneTaskIds; it did not touch id allocation.

Grep for the symbol rather than seeking to a line when you pick this up. Recorded because a line number that has silently moved reads exactly like one that has not.
finalSummary:
Draft, milestone and decision ids now allocate refs-aware, closing the last of the three id allocators QCLI-279 deliberately left open pending a real reproduction. That reproduction is the DEC-3 collision of 2026-09-14 this task documents.

AC1 -- decision recorded as DEC-7: both get refs-aware allocation, by two different mechanisms. Drafts reuse the existing filename scan against .quest/drafts and .quest/archive/drafts, since they are storage-identical to tasks. Milestones and decisions do not, and that is the substance of the task. Rejected alternatives are recorded there too: leaving them as-is (a live collision exists and recovery depended on the actor noticing), and a single unified helper branching on storage layout internally (it puts the one distinction that matters out of sight of both call sites).

AC2 -- implemented for all three families and demonstrated failing pre-fix. The pre-fix state IS mutant A (drafts) and mutant B (planning), and each reddens exactly the cases for its own family: 2 of 9 and 5 of 9 respectively, with no overlap. Nine tests, all driving real quest processes against real Git repositories, covering both trigger shapes -- unmerged sibling branch and detached HEAD behind a moved branch -- for each of the three families, plus prefix isolation, per-ref degradation, and the non-Git case.

THE FINDING WORTH CARRYING FORWARD, and the reason this was not a two-line change: the fix this task's own description proposed is silently wrong for half of it. highestSequenceOnOtherRefs finds ids by reading FILE NAMES, which works only because tasks and drafts are one record per file. Milestones and decisions share a single .quest/planning.json, so a filename scan over that path matches one file called planning.json, matches no id marker, and returns 0 -- indistinguishable from "no other ref carries a higher id". Measured rather than argued: a mutant implementing that obvious fix produces a verdict set byte-identical to a mutant with no fix at all, five of nine red, the same five. The wrong mechanism and the absent one are one observation, which is exactly why the obvious fix would have survived review. The planning half reads blob CONTENT per ref via the revision-pinned readBlob the Git port already exposed; no port change was required.

Five mutants, each predicted from the test file before running, all five matching: draft cross-ref term dropped -> 2 red; planning cross-ref term dropped -> 5 red; prefix filter dropped -> 1 red (a decision must not advance the milestone counter, though both live in one document); per-document parse guard dropped -> 1 red; the obvious fix -> the same 5 as no fix. The two single-red mutants redden DIFFERENT cases, which is what says the suite localises rather than pinning the implementation's identity.

A defect caught in my own test rather than in the code, recorded because the class recurs: the corrupt-ref case initially asserted only "sequential" and WOULD HAVE PASSED AGAINST THE BUG, because a guard coarse enough to abandon the whole scan on the first parse failure falls back to the local-only view, and local-only is sequential. It now uses three refs with one unparseable and asserts the exact id, so it is satisfied only if the scan skips that ref AND still reads the others. Mutant D exists to hold that.

AC3 -- quest instructions task-creation was part of the defect, not just undocumented. It promised the guarantee for tasks in wording a reader generalises to all four families, which is how DEC-3 happened. It now names all four families, records that the guarantee was narrower between the two releases, states the storage difference and that it is deliberately invisible to callers, and says ids minted earlier are not repaired by upgrading. CHANGELOG entry added under Unreleased/Fixed carrying the same bound.

AC4 -- bun run check exits 0: 558 pass, 0 fail, 4677 expect() calls across 64 files. lore check exits 0 (63 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings). The three pre-existing biome warnings are in test/promotion-fast-forward assertions and name none of the files changed here.

Unchanged in every other respect: local refs only and never a fetch, for-each-ref tips only and never a history walk, only a prefix's own family advances its counter, and a .quest directory with no Git repository behind it still allocates from the working tree alone.

Delivered as PR #161 into dev, head 3d44eea. CI on that exact head: Prepublication qualification run 35166370107 success, Tracker integrity run 35166370186 success, lore check run 35166369956 success. source-gates reported twice on that head -- once from pull_request and once from push, the source-touching case -- and both rows are completed success.
